cells.tense: You are here, pen down, letting what has finished finish.
cells.ask: Tell one person, plainly, what you accepted as finished this month, and what you are leaving open for that to become. Say only what you choose.
cells.core:
From where you stand you can take in the whole shape at once, and that is not the same as judging it. What is over reads as over to you, not as a verdict and not as an escape. You are not closing things to feel clean; you are letting them finish, and you trust that what comes after can be met. That is a quiet thing you carry, and it reaches the people around you in how you hold a room.
Fairness is doing something real here: what you have carried and what you are willing to put down are getting even, and the exchange happens in flow rather than by calculation. Say what has finished out loud. Let the renewal arrive on its own timing.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what is ending. Say it and let renewal in.
cells.verb: ending what has finished so something else can start
cells.place: where you can see the whole shape

cells.tense: You are already in the next upheaval, ending things before they can live.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you were about to end today and hold it one more week. Let someone in that situation see your face when you tell them why.
cells.core:
Every ending feels urgent, like the whole shape depends on getting ahead of it. Somewhere out there is a version where this is finally clear and you can rest, and you are living in that version instead of this one. The people beside you get a decision instead of you, and the closing keeps costing the thing it was meant to protect. Ending early is one more way of not arriving.
Compassion here is contact, not softness — let someone feel your actual state rather than a summary of what you have decided. Stay with one person long enough to know what they are carrying before you clear the table. The push to release early is fear wearing freedom's coat, and it reads plainly from outside.
cells.sheetLine: You are ending early to dodge the weight of staying.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that had already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Pick one object tied to something already finished and take it out of your space today. Ask one person to walk through that room with you and tell you what shifted.
cells.core:
Something has ended and you keep it where it was. You pass it every morning and call that steadiness. From outside it looks like loyalty, but the pattern you are known for spotting has gone cloudy around this one spot, and direction has nothing to run on while that space stays warm. The finished thing takes up room that something new would need.
Choose one object tied to what is over and move it out today. Let one person walk through that room with you and say what they notice. This is not about pushing feeling into a place that has gone quiet; it is one motion, small and concrete, so you can see again on your own.
cells.sheetLine: You keep a finished thing in place and call it steady.

cells.tense: You are already standing in the clearing, still calling it weather.
cells.ask: Name one thing that has already ended in your life but is still being handled as ongoing. Write it down somewhere private, then tell one person what you are no longer carrying.
cells.core:
The clearing is already underway and you have not named it. It shows up in how you talk about the last stretch — a rough season, a strange year — and not as something that finished. Taking in a whole shape is something you do constantly, and here you are doing it without letting yourself in on what you find. Naming the close would mean owning the change, so the talk stays about what keeps happening to you.
Say what is over but still being treated as ongoing. Write it down where only you will read it, then tell one person what you are no longer carrying. That statement is structure, and structure is what holds the next thing while it forms.
cells.sheetLine: You are in the clearing and calling it a rough year.
